recommendation: Do not implement a fold-statistic cache or request a census for this owner-identity hypothesis. Source structure already makes the key injective on the reachable fold list for each fixed opponent. This is not a claim about equal row contents or cross-iteration caching.
question: D055 README line33 deferred repeated fold-statistic reuse because useful duplicate reach owners had not been established. D062 examines that exact within-sweep identity question, without executing a census.

safe_key_and_value.key: Within one completed downward reach generation and one fixed plan/workspace: opponent player q, reach allocation/generation, reach_slot[q][fold_node], and the immutable hand/card-list layout. Slot number alone across players, solvers or swapped workspaces is unsafe.
safe_key_and_value.value: T plus s[0..52), 53 f32 words (212 bytes) per distinct key; this excludes any index/validity metadata. same_r remains the original opponent-row lookup and amount remains per terminal.
safe_key_and_value.exact_order: Retain block128, +0 initialization, each card ascending original card_idx loop, thread-strided total partials and the original 64/32/.../1 tree. Retain ((T-s[c1])-s[c2])+same_r then amount multiplication. A separate producer would need exact round/store/reload behavior and raw-bit proof; no such implementation or proof is supplied.

injectivity_proof.claim: TreeBuilder emits fresh child nodes, with at most one Fold action at a decision. Fold is available only while facing a bet. First Check and every Bet/Raise switch actor; Call and second Check terminate the street into showdown or chance. A new action round follows a chance edge.
For fixed opponent q, every q action edge creates a new owner equal to its child node; every chance edge creates a new owner for both players. Only the other player action edge preserves q owner.
If q folds, the fold terminal owns its q reach row and has no descendants. Distinct such folds have distinct fresh node IDs and cannot share their owner with another fold.

If the other player p folds, it inherits q owner from its decision. Before another p decision can be reached, action alternation requires a q action edge or a chance edge; either changes q owner. Since each p decision has at most one Fold, no second p-fold can retain the same q owner. Branching into several q decisions does not help: their fold edges and any paths to another p decision first change q owner.

Iso selects representative chance subtrees and fold_nodes includes reached nodes only; it does not merge distinct active owner IDs. reach_slot assigns a separate slot per owner, with no reach-row scratch reuse. Inactive default-owner entries therefore do not create fold-list collisions.

structural_conclusion.within_fixed_opponent_and_sweep: Every reachable fold terminal has a distinct reach_slot; owner-key duplicate groups have size1.
structural_conclusion.basis: Source deduction for current TreeBuilder-produced trees, not an executed fixture census or timing measurement. Publicly constructed/mutated nonstandard Trees with consecutive same-player decisions are outside this proof; no such production construction was found (Tree literal centralized in tree.rs416).

lifetime_limits: During one upward sweep, reach arrays are read-only, so an otherwise valid owner-key statistic could remain valid across levels. That lifetime does not create duplicate owners.

E015 reuses reach1 only in the second paired downward pass; p0 fold uses reach1 while p1 fold uses newly computed reach0. This is not a shared opponent row between the two fold traversals. Following training/evaluation downward passes may rewrite rows.

Raked evaluation already computes terminals once per player and reuses their full CFVs in the second mode (mod.rs521-537,628-630). Recomputing or caching only fold statistics cannot eliminate that already absent second calculation.

Warm state, locks, new root inputs and errors require generation-aware invalidation for any cross-pass cache. Standalone continuation uploads roots then takes a full sweep (mod.rs178-194,759-772). Host/SSD paging swaps d_reach among seven mutable buffers; plan slot equality does not identify physical contents across swaps.
cost_and_scope: With no repeated key within a sweep, an owner-index table and 212-byte statistic records add work/storage without removing the original per-owner reductions. This is a mechanism-level no-go, not a measured complete-cycle claim and not proof that all conceivable fold optimizations fail. No E019 reduction variant, E030 card scheduling variant or E032 terminal scheduling variant is reopened.
census_decision: No new CPU-only census recommended now. If TreeBuilder semantics later change, the smallest structural check is fold_nodes grouped by reach_slot[q] for each q on a finalized GpuPlan, reporting node/owner identities and group multiplicities. That contingency is neither prepared nor authorized here.
exploration_note: One read-only rg command used a Windows wildcard path that rg treated literally; repeated required lookup with concrete files. No source change or execution occurred.
